items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include badged review-body findings in validation**

Badged top-level review findings never reach the validation loop because `scripts/pr-feedback.py:191-200` creates every `review` item with `path` and `line` unset, while this predicate requires both. Thus, even with `DISPOSITIONS_REQUIRE_REFUTATION=1`, such a finding can retain legacy or otherwise unverified `not-applicable` evidence and the gate still succeeds; parse its blob location or at minimum require its refutation without relying on these fields. The threat-table test only exercises `review_comment` items, so it does not close the declared review-item control.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L75-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/74baf481b5c9946dc4f98eed4507f564e000f433/AGENTS.md#L75-L78)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Pass feedback paths as literal pathspecs**

When a PR contains a legal filename beginning with `:`, this argument is interpreted by Git as pathspec magic rather than as the literal GitHub path; for example an exclude/glob path can make `hunks()` inspect unrelated files or no file and incorrectly accept `diff:` evidence. The [Git glossary](https://git-scm.com/docs/gitglossary#Documentation/gitglossary.txt-aiddefpathspecapathspec) specifies this leading-colon behavior. Prefix the untrusted path with Git's literal pathspec form before every diff/log call; the current closed-row test uses only `a.py`, so it does not exercise this trust-boundary case.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L75-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/74baf481b5c9946dc4f98eed4507f564e000f433/AGENTS.md#L75-L78)
